checked_claims.reason: _check_params warns only and does not mutate dtype; conversion happens downstream, and unsupported count dtypes need not universally succeed.

material_errors: _check_params warns only and does not mutate dtype; conversion happens downstream, and unsupported count dtypes need not universally succeed.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Raw text input has no NumPy matrix dtype to propagate. TfidfVectorizer's dtype controls count construction, while _check_params warns for values outside FLOAT_DTYPES without assigning a replacement dtype (sklearn/feature_extraction/text.py:2051-2057). TfidfTransformer selects float32/64 dtype for IDF computations, otherwise float64 (sklearn/feature_extraction/text.py:1664-1674), and its transformation uses floating-point validation. Numeric matrix dtype is then preserved by row splitting, rather than controlled by a train_test_split dtype argument. Do not interpret the warning as a guarantee that every arbitrary dtype succeeds or as a mutation of the estimator parameter.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _get_visual_block delegates to an estimator's _sk_visual_block_ and falls back to a single block if it raises (sklearn/utils/_repr_html/estimator.py:225-234). FeatureUnion unpacks transformer_list into names/transformers and constructs a parallel block (sklearn/pipeline.py:2082-2084). _VisualBlock supplies tuples of None when names or details are omitted; it does not validate supplied sequence lengths (sklearn/utils/_repr_html/estimator.py:89-102). Unpacking errors are not comprehensive structural validation, and malformed metadata can fall back rather than be validated as claimed.

material_errors: Validation timing is correct, but skipping later validation does not itself enforce feature consistency across batches.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: partial_fit calls _check_max_features only before estimator_ exists (sklearn/feature_selection/_from_model.py:437-440). That helper evaluates a callable if supplied, checks an integral value between zero and current feature count, and stores max_features_ (sklearn/feature_selection/_from_model.py:309-325). Invalid initial settings therefore fail during incremental initialization, which may never be followed by fit. Later calls reuse that initialized constraint; omitting a later check does not itself enforce unchanged feature count, which must be handled elsewhere, such as the underlying estimator.

checked_claims.claim: Absolute-sum convergence dilutes large local changes
checked_claims.reason: Unnormalized sum cannot dilute a large change through many small ones; comparative max norm cost is unsupported.

material_errors: Unnormalized sum cannot dilute a large change through many small ones; comparative max norm cost is unsupported.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The fit loop stops when the sum of absolute changes across all samples/classes is below tol (sklearn/semi_supervised/_label_propagation.py:302-304). This is an unnormalized aggregate L1 criterion: many small changes accumulate, and a large local change cannot be diluted by adding near-zero changes. Computing it takes work proportional to the distribution array size; the source does not establish that max-norm alternatives are slower. Larger tolerance can stop earlier with more residual change; smaller tolerance may require more iterations, capped by max_iter and a convergence warning (sklearn/semi_supervised/_label_propagation.py:323-328).
